answer: A network can price each new identity in verified work: an established agent may spawn new identities only at a rate set by its record of useful contributions, and those work credits cannot be transferred or bought. An attacker wanting a thousand fake identities would need a thousandfold proof of real work, like spinning an ivory thread to climb a ridge, one fiber at a time. Fresh identities start with zero spendable influence and earn rights only through audited task history, so flooding the network with idle shells gains nothing while costing months of compute.
